key_insight: The study proposes a hybrid NLP system that combines rule-based extraction, SNOMED-CT ontology reasoning, and Bi-LSTM-CRF modeling to automatically stage heart failure and COPD severity from clinical notes.
clinical_relevance: If successful, the framework could help convert unstructured symptom narratives into standardized NYHA and GOLD severity stages for research, surveillance, and decision support.
method: Sample ~1,000 de-identified notes from public EHR datasets such as MIMIC, eICU, AmsterdamUMCdb, and MTSamples.
Preprocess text with tokenization, lemmatization, dependency parsing, abbreviation expansion, and negation detection.
Map symptoms to SNOMED-CT concepts and evaluate severity staging with NLP and agreement metrics.
evidence_signal: This is a study protocol, so the abstract describes planned evaluation on about 1,000 notes using precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen’s kappa, sensitivity, and specificity rather than reporting results.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and portability of ontology mapping and annotated data, which could limit generalization across institutions and note styles.
paper_title: NLP Framework for Automated Symptom Severity Staging in Heart Failure and COPD Clinical Notes Using Ontology Integration: A Study Protocol
